* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

homes near the intersection of Navajo Route 2 and Navajo Route 71
are conducted.

Winslow, Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres, Homolovi
Ruins State Park and Clear Creek Reservoir.

properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:53PM MST until November 4 at 4:00PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River continues.

* WHAT...Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River,
caused by recent runoff from upstream rain and snowmelt, is
occurring.

* WHERE...Eastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
West Central Costilla County in south central Colorado...
South Central Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Conejos River, from Mogote downstream
to Manassa, and the San Antonio River, near Ortiz downstream to
Manassa, is ongoing. Additional flooding of creeks, streams, and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations is possible. Numerous
roads remain closed due to flooding. Expect many areas of slow
moving or standing water through eastern Conejos County.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 347 PM MST, Upstream runoff from recent rain and snowmelt is
causing flooding into eastern Conejos County.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford, Antonito, Romeo, Alamosa East, Conejos and
Ortiz.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Montezuma, CO; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:31PM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the San Juan River caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...along the San Juan River from the Four Corners through
Mexican Hat, UT. This includes Bluff, Montezuma Creek and Aneth.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM MST, stream gauge reports upstream and impacts of
flooding have been reported along the San Juan River near
Farmington, NM. Expect flood waters to reach the Four Corners
Wednesday evening and the town of Bluff early Thursday morning.
Timing of crest is subject to change as more details become
available. Please continue to monitor the forecast and updated
warnings.
- At 11:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 22 feet late this evening with
a secondary crest near 23.5 feet expected near Bluff early
Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Bluff, Montezuma Creek, and Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
